_meta.title: Value Compass - Scored Maker Dataset
_meta.polarity: ALL axes scored 0-4 where HIGHER = more pro-social (more transparent, better culture/ESG, more labour & supply-chain integrity, more dispersed ownership, more public wealth-sharing, more open weights and source availability). A high-scoring maker draws a large polygon on the compass.

confidence.A: strong / externally validated (e.g., FMTI score exists)
confidence.B: moderate / some primary disclosure or credible reporting

axis_aliases.wealth_dispersion: your 'wealth distribution' axis, higher = more dispersed

key_anchors.transparency: Stanford FMTI 2025 (avg 40.69/100; IBM 95 high; xAI & Midjourney 14 low). 0-4 mapping: 0=<=12, 1=13-29, 2=30-49, 3=50-74, 4=>=75.
key_anchors.environmental_note: FMTI 2025 found 10 of 13 firms disclose NOTHING on energy/carbon/water - the environmental sub-indicator is near-zero sector-wide.
key_anchors.labour_benchmark: Global-South data labelers commonly earn ~$1.50-2/hr; OpenAI/Sama Kenya is the canonical documented case.
key_anchors.open_weights: DRAFT scale from the 2026-10-30 research pack (art_zYCpqJCa Part B), recorded for review: 4 = weights under a permissive OSI-style license (Apache/MIT); 3 = weights with conditions (community license, modified MIT, non-commercial CC); 2 = no own weights but substantial open product/client/tool code; 1 = no weights, peripheral open-source artifacts only; 0 = no weights and no meaningful source found (scoped to a research pass); n/a = not established. Independent of transparency BY DESIGN: FMTI 2025 scored Alibaba 26/100 despite Apache 2.0 Qwen releases — read the two axes separately. Scores on this axis are recorded against the draft scale and stay decision-ineligible until the rubric adopts the scale as a rule.

_meta.products_note: products_models are listed inside each maker node for filtering/comparison; they are NOT separate nodes.
_meta.join_key: Each maker has an 'id' (short name). funders[].makers_backed and owns_outright reference makers by this id. Join on id, NOT on display 'name'.
_meta.capital_profile_note: Each maker has a factual 'capital_profile' (objective attributes). The Capital Lens (user-configurable) decides which attributes count as concerns; it is NOT a fixed 6th score.
_meta.last_freshness_review: 2026-06-13: verified xAI/SpaceX (closed Feb 2026), Anthropic ($965B Series H + confidential IPO), OpenAI (Oct 2025 recapitalization), Cohere/Aleph Alpha (announced Apr 2026), DeepSeek (~$7.4B round near closing + V4), Meta (Muse Spark closed-weight pivot Apr 2026), Moonshot (~$10B+). Tool-layer valuations are date-stamped (late 2025-early 2026) and were not re-verified individually.

makers.name: Anthropic
makers.structure: Public Benefit Corporation; Long-Term Benefit Trust
makers.stated_values: Safety-first, beneficial AI at the frontier; Constitutional AI; interpretability.
makers.tension_hook: Safety-first framing vs. participating in the same capability/compute race it warns about.

transparency.note: Most transparent frontier lab in FMTI 2025 (rose to 2nd of the 6 longitudinal firms) but still only industry-typical; opaque on data/compute/environment.

culture_esg.note: Strong mission-aligned culture and unusually robust governance (PBC + Long-Term Benefit Trust); but zero environmental disclosure like all peers.

labour_integrity.note: Relies on outsourced RLHF/labeling vendors with no public disclosure; no major documented abuses, but supply chain is opaque.

wealth_dispersion.note: Economics heavily concentrated in Amazon (~15-19%) and Google (~14%); the trust governs mission, not the cap table.

public_sharing.note: PBC + Long-Term Benefit Trust as binding structure; founders signed the Giving Pledge; paid-access model limits free reach.

open_weights.note: Not scored. No public disclosure of an open-weight Claude release was located in the 2026-10-30 research pass — a scoped absence in our record, not a statement about the company. Research gap: the peripheral open-source inventory (SDKs and samples) that would separate the pack's provisional 1 from 0 was not verified.

capital_profile.note: Factual capital attributes (objective). Whether any of these is a 'concern' is the user's call via the Capital Lens.

makers.name: OpenAI
makers.structure: For-profit PBC (OpenAI Group) controlled by the nonprofit OpenAI Foundation; recapitalized Oct 2025 (capped-profit model scrapped)
makers.stated_values: Ensure AGI benefits all of humanity; broad distribution of benefits.
makers.tension_hook: 'Benefit all humanity' nonprofit origins vs. for-profit restructuring, founder departures, and commercial pace.

transparency.note: FMTI 2025 middle group but declined ~14 points; near the bottom of the firms tracked all three years; limited o3 disclosure.

culture_esg.note: Repeated governance turmoil (2023 board crisis, safety-team departures) and a contested for-profit conversion, completed Oct 2025; environmental non-disclosure.

labour_integrity.note: Documented Kenya/Sama case: moderators paid ~$2/hr to review violent content with inadequate support.

wealth_dispersion.note: After the Oct 2025 recapitalization the nonprofit OpenAI Foundation holds ~26% and controls the board, Microsoft ~27%, and ~47% sits with employees and investors - control rests with the nonprofit and economics are moderately spread (no single holder >27%), not capped.

public_sharing.note: Scrapped its binding 'capped-profit' sharing mechanism in the Oct 2025 for-profit conversion. What remains is nonprofit control plus the OpenAI Foundation's ~26% (~$130B) stake funding philanthropy (health, AI resilience) - real machinery, but removing the profit cap is a live stated-vs-observed gap against the 'benefit all of humanity' claim.

open_weights.note: gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b are open-weight reasoning models released 2025-08-05 under the Apache 2.0 license together with the gpt-oss usage policy (verified against the model card). The flagship GPT models remain closed, capping below 4.

makers.name: StackBlitz (Bolt)
makers.vc_independent: Privately held. A 2022 seed round was announced; no current cap table is established.
makers.structure: Privately held. Identified as Bolt's operator by Bolt's own privacy policy.
makers.stated_values: Publishes an open-source fund reporting $82.2K in direct maintainer sponsorship during 2025 and announcing an expanded monthly programme for 2026.
makers.tension_hook: Funds independent open-source maintainers while announcing that customer content will be used for model development and dataset licensing from October 2026 outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland.

transparency.note: Publishes unusually detailed product-data disclosures: a Model training setting that is on by default except for accounts based in the EU, UK, or Switzerland (off by default there), applying to content submitted on or after 7 October 2026, with Enterprise/Team customers under an MSA or DPA excluded from training ("A new Model training setting in your account settings lets you choose whether Bolt can use your projects and chats to train AI models. It's on by default, except for accounts based in the EU, UK, or Switzerland, where it's off by default" — verified verbatim 2026-10-30). Bolt Forge (announced 2026-09-14) turns opt-in coding sessions into de-identified datasets "Bolt.new licenses to AI developers, starting with Arcee AI"; switching off Forge does not delete previously collected data — users must request removal. Scoring caveat: this is product-level disclosure — StackBlitz is not a foundation-model developer, and the axis's model-building sub-indicators (data provenance, labour, compute) have nothing on record because the company builds no model.

culture_esg.note: Not scored. No credible dated evidence of layoffs, workplace-review aggregates, environmental disclosure or governance issues was found in the 2026-10-30 research pass; absence of findings is not a clean record (research gap).

labour_integrity.note: Not scored. The relevant record is user-contributed data labour, not vendor labour: Bolt's Model training setting is opt-out by default for most accounts (on by default except EU/UK/CH), and Bolt Forge opt-in sessions go into datasets licensed to AI developers ("the allocation is the payment" — extra usage, with no cash compensation or revenue share documented) (2026-09/10, verified 2026-10-30). A third-party trust assessment reads the terms as granting "a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, sublicensable, and transferable license" over model-development content — third-party interpretation; check the primary terms before legal use. No conventional data-labour vendors, wages or litigation were found; the axis stays not established.

wealth_dispersion.note: A $105.5M Series B was announced 2025-01-22, led by Emergence and GV with participation from Madrona, The Chainsmokers (Mantis), Conviction and others (company announcement, verified 2026-10-30); Bloomberg (2025-01-21) reported talks at a ~$700M valuation. Any Founders Fund participation is not confirmed by this pass. The full cap table, earlier rounds and employee-equity breadth are not established.

public_sharing.note: Reports $82,200 paid directly to open-source maintainers during 2025 through its open-source fund (company-reported), with an expanded monthly programme for 2026 announced rather than completed; neither is a fixed share of revenue nor a binding structure.

open_weights.note: bolt.diy — the official open source version of Bolt.new — is published under the MIT license, while the hosted Bolt product and the WebContainers runtime stay proprietary (the WebContainer API needs a commercial license in production). No model weights.

capital_profile.note: Factual capital attributes (objective). Whether any of these is a 'concern' is the user's call via the Capital Lens.

transparency.note: Vercel publishes a documented account of v0's training data: "v0 was trained on a large corpus of data from various sources, including third parties listed in Vercel's AI Policy", with v0 Enterprise content and opted-out customers excluded, prompt/content download offered, and the caveat that "if any or your inputs and outputs were used to train existing v0 models, those models will not be updated" (docs FAQ, last updated 2026-03-17; verified verbatim 2026-10-30). Set against this, an anonymous employee review alleges layoffs were kept quiet internally (Glassdoor, 2023-01-06). Vercel is not a foundation-model developer — no FMTI anchor; manual score.

culture_esg.note: Layoffs around early 2023 are supported only by an anonymous 2023-01-06 Glassdoor review ("Was laid off with some of my colleagues and it seems to be kept quiet throughout the whole company"); no company announcement or WARN-verified headcount data was found for 2022-2024, so no yearly layoff sequence is asserted. Anonymous culture signals are mixed and unquantified: "It's celebrated to be working on weekends and late nights"; one review calls the environment "cultish". Perception signals from a single source — fragile; a second source would move this either way.

labour_integrity.note: Not scored. The relevant record is customer-content training terms, not vendor labour: v0 "may use user-generated prompts and/or content as inputs to models and learning systems from third-party providers to improve our products", with Enterprise content excluded and opt-outs not retroactive (docs FAQ, verified verbatim 2026-10-30); no compensation to users whose content improves models is documented. No data-labour vendors or litigation were found; the axis stays not established.

wealth_dispersion.note: Reported financing: Series E of $250M at a $3.25B post-money valuation (May 2024, Accel-led); Series F of $300M at $9.3B (September 2025, co-led by Accel and GIC), reportedly including a ~$300M tender offer providing liquidity to early investors, employees and former employees; ~$863M disclosed total. No reliable public evidence that the founder holds majority voting control or super-voting shares — third-party synthesis, verify against filings (research pass 2026-10-30).

public_sharing.note: Publishes a portfolio of open-source projects it maintains or contributes to, including the Next.js framework and the AI SDK — software other businesses rely on; the record notes this is a different contribution from funding independent maintainers, and no structural public-benefit commitment is on record.

open_weights.note: Next.js, Turbopack and the AI SDK are open source — the AI SDK is 'a free open-source library' built and maintained by Vercel (verified 2026-10-30) — while v0 is a hosted, closed product and no model weights are published.

transparency.note: Not scored. The batch research (docs/RESEARCH_BATCH.md, 2026-09-27) recorded no disclosure-practices finding for Proton; the Foundation's 1% revenue transfers are not published in any year (see tension hook), and no assessment of overall disclosure practices is on record. Absence of findings is not a clean record.

culture_esg.note: The batch's only conduct finding: after the CEO's January 2025 post about US politics was deleted following criticism, Proton described the episode as an internal miscommunication and set a policy of sharing no opinions of a political nature. The finding concerns company communications rather than the treatment of workers; no workplace or environmental matter was found in the window, and absence of findings is not a clean record.

labour_integrity.note: Not scored. Inherited exposure: Lumo runs on third-party frontier models whose upstream labour it does not control; the batch research (docs/RESEARCH_BATCH.md, 2026-09-27) established no direct data-worker or creator finding for Proton, and absence of findings is not a clean record.

wealth_dispersion.note: Not scored. Majority ownership by the non-profit Proton Foundation is on record (see vc_independent), but backer concentration, employee equity breadth and pay dispersion are not established, and the rubric states no rule for combining ownership structure into a 0–4 score.

public_sharing.note: Majority-owned by the non-profit Proton Foundation, which receives 1% of Proton's revenues for charitable activities whenever financial conditions allow, with over $5m in grants reported to date; the amounts transferred in any year are not published, and the commitment is conditional rather than binding.

open_weights.note: Not scored. The pack records client apps as open source and Lumo as serving third-party open-weight models hosted in the EU, but the specific repositories and the Lumo model list were not verified (research gap) — no score without a verifiable source.

makers.name: Alibaba Group
makers.jurisdiction: Cayman Islands incorporation, headquartered in Hangzhou, China
makers.vc_independent: Publicly traded. No venture backer holds it.
makers.structure: Alibaba Group Holding Limited, a Cayman Islands company listed on the New York Stock Exchange (BABA) and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (9988).
makers.stated_values: Not researched.
makers.tension_hook: A listed company answerable to public shareholders, operating Qwen from China — two different sets of obligations on the same product.

transparency.note: Stanford FMTI 2025 scored Alibaba 26/100 — one of four developers scored for the first time ("This includes two Chinese companies (DeepSeek, Alibaba) both of whom score poorly (at 32 and 26) despite releasing open-weight models", verified verbatim 2026-10-30). Under the band mapping in _meta.key_anchors.transparency (1 = 13-29), 26 maps to 1. The FMTI company report (run against the Qwen 3 technical report) scores data-acquisition methods 0 — "The developer does not make methods for acquiring pretraining data adequately clear" — and awards 0 to training energy, carbon-emissions and water disclosure. Open weights do not make transparency: this is the rubric §1 warning, confirmed with numbers.

culture_esg.note: Corporate commitments on record: in December 2021 Alibaba announced Scope 1 and 2 carbon neutrality by 2030, a 50% Scope 3 carbon-intensity reduction by 2030 (vs 2020), carbon-neutral Alibaba Cloud across Scopes 1-3 by 2030, and a "Scope 3+" aim to facilitate 1.5 gigatons of ecosystem decarbonization by 2035. Set against that, FMTI 2025 found no energy, carbon or water reporting for AI model training (company report scores 0 on all three) and describes a governance advisory board whose deployment recommendations are nonbinding. Independent verification of the Scope 3 accounting is not established; current working-hour practices were not researched in this pass (see labour_integrity).

labour_integrity.note: Not scored. The 2026-10-30 research pass found no sourced, dated evidence on the pay, terms or subcontracting of data workers in the Qwen training pipeline, and no labour litigation involving Alibaba's AI data labelling was located either. The FMTI 2025 company report scores data-laborer practices 0 and data-acquisition methods 0, which establishes that the supply chain is undisclosed — under the rubric that is nondisclosure, not a documented condition, so no score is entered (research gap).

wealth_dispersion.note: Widely held public company (NYSE: BABA; HKEX: 9988) with an internal Alibaba Partnership that nominates a substantial portion of board candidates — founder influence through nomination rights rather than majority economic ownership (structure as reported 2018). Current Ma/Tsai stakes, partnership composition and the final terms and timing of SoftBank's exit are not established from filings (research pass 2026-10-30) — industry-typical dispersion is the interim read, pending a current exchange filing.

public_sharing.note: The Jack Ma Foundation (founded 15 December 2014; education, entrepreneurship, women's leadership, medical support, environment) and the Alibaba Foundation (December 2011, funded with a stated percentage of Alibaba's annual income) are on record. Rural-education giving: the Rural Teacher Initiative selected 100 teachers/year at 100,000 yuan each (UN, 2016); a $30M 10-year rural-teaching pledge (BBC, 2018); company-reported totals of at least $75M pledged and $300M+ distributed or pledged (Forbes Kazakhstan, 2020 — not independently verified). Caution: most headline figures attach to the Jack Ma Foundation personally, not to Alibaba Group as maker. Qwen's open-weight releases are a public-interest output. No binding wealth-sharing structure (no trust/PBC/windfall clause) is on record.

open_weights.note: Principal Qwen3 releases (from 2025-04-29) ship under Apache 2.0 with unconditional commercial use, while legacy Tongyi Qianwen checkpoints (e.g. Qwen2.5-72B) carry a >100M-MAU trigger and attribution requirement — recorded per checkpoint, not family-wide (third-party source, verified 2026-10-30). Openness here is not a transparency measure: FMTI 2025 scored Alibaba 26/100 despite these Apache 2.0 releases.

capital_profile.note: Factual capital attributes (objective). Whether any of these is a 'concern' is the user's call via the Capital Lens. A public parent is held by passive index funds; this is not an operational tie to a Big Tech owner.

makers.name: DuckDuckGo
makers.jurisdiction: United States (Duck Duck Go, Inc., Paoli, Pennsylvania)
makers.vc_independent: Venture-backed. Self-funded by its founder until a Series A led by Union Square Ventures in October 2011.
lead_backers: Union Square Ventures (led the October 2011 Series A)
makers.structure: Privately held US company. Duck Duck Go, Inc.
makers.stated_values: Search and browsing without tracking; revenue from advertising and, since April 2024, subscriptions.
makers.tension_hook: A privacy company whose AI chat runs on models built by OpenAI, Anthropic and Mistral — its own privacy terms sit in front of someone else's model.

transparency.note: Duck.ai names its model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Azure, and open models such as gpt-oss-120b and Gemma hosted via Tinfoil), shows the active model to users, and publishes retention/training rules per provider: "By default, Duck.ai does not record or store any of your chats, and your conversations are not used to train chat models by DuckDuckGo or the underlying model providers (for example, Open AI and Anthropic)" (verified verbatim 2026-10-30). Exceptions are documented: optional feedback can store a conversation; Sync & Backup stores chats end-to-end encrypted; OpenAI/Anthropic may hold chats in short-term memory (up to 1 hour, never written to disk) or retain where required by law; output-removal requests route to the provider. Caveats: safeguards rest partly on private provider agreements that are not published for inspection, and DuckDuckGo is not a foundation-model developer — no FMTI anchor, so this is a manual score on the rubric's six sub-indicators.

culture_esg.note: Company reporting describes a deliberately lean hiring culture: "never in the company history, we were forced to do any group layoffs" and a stated 95% employee retention rate (Duck Tales ep. 12, 2025-12-10 — self-reported, not independently verified, and silent on individual role eliminations). The 2026-10-30 pass found no environmental disclosure to credit the environmental sub-indicator.

labour_integrity.note: Not scored. DuckDuckGo trains no frontier model in-house — Duck.ai serves third-party models under contract (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Azure, Tinfoil-hosted open models) — so no data-labour or moderation supply chain of its own is on record; no labour litigation was found in the 2026-10-30 pass. Structural note, not a scored finding (research gap).

wealth_dispersion.note: Bootstrapped until Union Square Ventures led the October 2011 Series A — a $3-5M range per contemporaneous reporting, with angel participation and a USV managing partner joining the board — so the folklore that DuckDuckGo took no outside investment is false as a general claim. No further rounds were found in the 2026-10-30 pass. What USV or founder Gabriel Weinberg hold today is not established: the company is private and no current cap table is public.

public_sharing.note: Company-reported giving: duckduckgo.com/donations itemizes "over $9,050,000" donated since 2011 to privacy, open-source, tech-journalism and data-rights organizations ("over a million dollars to, I think this year it was something like 29 different organizations" — company podcast ep. 13, 2025-12-10). Self-reported and not audited, though itemized by organization and year; no binding structure (no trust/PBC/windfall clause) is on record.

open_weights.note: Duck.ai's free lineup includes open-weight third-party models (gpt-oss-120b, Gemma 4 31B) hosted by Tinfoil.sh (verified 2026-10-30), and client/tooling code is open source (e.g. AutoConsent) — but serving open models is not the same as releasing own weights, and DuckDuckGo trains no frontier model, so the score caps at 2.
